newsitem.title: USA: BankBoston to open Peru branch.
newsitem.headline: BankBoston to open Peru branch.

text.p: BankBoston said it is seeking the approval of Peruvian authorities to open a branch in Lima by mid-October.
The new office will deliver credit, trade services, custody, treasury services, corporate finance and cash management services to multinationals and to large, locally-based corporate customers.

"Peru has evolved from the most highly regulated country in Latin America in the 1980's to one of the region's most open, private sector-friendly countries today," chief executive Chad Gifford said in a statement. "Peru had the fastest growing economy in Latin America during the 1994-1995 period, and we are delighted that we are now in a position to provide local banking services in this very attractive market."
The office will be headed by General Manager Rafael Venegas, a Peruvian banker with extensive international banking experience. Venegas will report to BankBoston group executive Mark MacLennan.
Opening the office will require the approval of Peru's superintendent of banks, BankBoston said.
